Core curriculum — Insight Foundations, Insight Bootcamp, Overview of Capabilities, Culture in Action, the Leadership Model, the 360s course, Writing with Impact, and ExI Bootcamp. Assessment — shadow full ALPs; lead 360 interviews and write the page solo; write ISP and capabilities pages; write strengths, development opportunities, and summary pages; build toward delivering a full ALP report at roughly 80 percent client readiness. Organizational consulting — administer and analyze ISP, culture, and team effectiveness surveys; draft group and culture reports; debrief the culture graph; support workshop design, materials, and onsite coordination. Business acumen — how businesses make money, different operating and ownership models, organizational structures, C-suite roles and responsibilities, and basic financial literacy. This is supported by the LAS Business Acumen Series (Business Strategy, Financial Basics, Anatomy of a Company, Engagement and Client Management). Consulting skills — craft a credible introduction for clients, present informed opinions and defend them with data, professionally challenge the views of others, and proactively seek feedback from every project team. THE SUPPORT AROUND YOU You will not be left to figure this out alone. Every new Associate is supported by a defined team: Talent Partner — your manager, responsible for your development, staffing, and performance, with a recurring one-on-one cadence Onboarding mentor — a peer who helps you navigate the Firm, its systems, and its unwritten rules Apprenticeship mentors — one to two Associates or Senior Associates who are your first point of contact for client work; new hires are paired with a dedicated Consultant or Senior Associate capacity for the first six to twelve months, so you learn by apprenticeship Engagement teams — Consultants, Associates, and Executive Engagement Assistants who coach you in the flow of the work The AAPM community — the Associate & Analyst Practice Member group, which runs monthly calls, coffee chats, learning cafés, and peer development programming THE REALITIES OF THE ROLE We would rather be direct than have you discover these after you join. The workload is deadline-driven and uneven. Priorities are set by client needs and Consultant schedules. There are genuinely intense stretches around report deadlines, board readouts, and workshops, and quieter stretches in between. This is client service: timelines shift, clients reschedule, and there will be occasional work outside normal hours to meet a client commitment. Assessment work is rigorous. Spending several hours on camera with a participant and then multiple hours writing and nuancing a report is demanding. It is also core to what we do. We balance assessment with other work to give you a variety. Staffing is partially relationship-based. Opportunities are influenced by the connections, trust, and internal reputation you build. Early on, you will work on what the practice needs, which may not always be the work that energizes you most. Over time, you gain far more influence over the projects and people you work with, but you have to invest in the relationships to get there. The work is predominantly at the most senior levels. Because we work with C-suite executives and boards, there are fewer opportunities to independently lead assessments early on than at firms that work deeper in the organization. This also leads to what makes the role great (below). Autonomy can feel like ambiguity. You will be trusted to manage your own time and to choose work in partnership with your Talent Partner. Not every step will be laid out for you. The learning curve is real. Our methodology is complex, and our quality bar is high. Most Associates, including those with directly relevant prior experience, need several months before they feel confident with the tools, frameworks, and standards. That is expected. WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE WORTH IT Exposure to senior leaders and consequential decisions. Associates work directly on material that reaches C-suite executives, boards, and investors, and contributes to decisions that shape organizations. That exposure typically comes much later in a career elsewhere. Accelerated learning. You will see how successful leaders think, make decisions, and navigate complexity across many companies, industries, and situations in a fraction of the time it would take from inside a single organization. Exceptional colleagues. Our people are consistently named as the best part of working here: smart, generous with their time, deeply committed to quality, and invested in helping one another improve. Quality over volume. We prioritize thoughtful analysis, sound judgment, and exceptional work products over speed or scale. That creates a steeper learning curve and a far better development experience. Variety and breadth. Public and private companies across every major sector, and work spanning assessment, succession, culture, team effectiveness, development, and organizational effectiveness. Real ownership. You own workstreams, deliverables and client communications, and you have meaningful influence over your schedule, your projects and your career path. A developmental culture. Structured curriculum, apprenticeship mentoring, real-time feedback on every project, a published development framework and colleagues who are invested in your growth rather than competing with you. KEY RELATIONSHIPS Reports to Talent Partner (Leadership Advisory Services) Day-to-day direction Consultants and Senior Associates, on a per-engagement basis Career guidance Counselor (Consultant), onboarding mentor and apprenticeship mentors Other key relationships Analysts; Project Managers; Executive Engagement Assistants; Content Editors; Client Care Liaisons; Knowledge Management and Solution Support; Executive Search colleagues; the Associate & Analyst Practice Member (AAPM) community Location Based in one of our North American offices CANDIDATE PROFILE IDEAL EXPERIENCE Generally four or more years of relevant professional experience in leadership advisory, executive assessment, management or strategy consulting, organizational development, human capital or talent management, or a relevant industry role. Undergraduate degree from an accredited institution. An advanced degree (for example, in organizational psychology, industrial-organizational psychology, business or a related field) is helpful but not required; relevant professional experience can substitute. Superior business writing skills, evidenced through project work or a writing sample provided on request Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex qualitative and quantitative information into clear, evidence-based insight Strong project management and organizational skills, with a track record of managing multiple priorities and competing deadlines General business acumen developed through exposure to a range of business situations and contexts Executive presence and interpersonal effectiveness; comfort interacting with senior leaders Client deliverables are written in English; superior English business writing is an essential function of the role. Additional languages are an advantage. Work authorization for the country in which you are applying WHO TENDS TO THRIVE HERE Intellectually curious people who want to understand the “why” behind people, businesses, and organizational outcomes, and who enjoy connecting disparate pieces of information into a point of view People who combine intellectual confidence with genuine humility, and who engage readily with feedback and iteration Strong writers and communicators who take visible pride in the quality of their work and the accuracy of their details Self-directed people who are comfortable creating structure where none exists, figuring things out independently, and taking ownership of their own career Resourceful relationship builders who proactively reach out, build trust across teams, and adapt their style to different personalities and Consultant preferences People who are comfortable with ambiguity, shifting priorities, and the pace of client service Team-oriented colleagues with a “no task too small” mindset who contribute beyond their immediate responsibilities People with poise, maturity, and professional presence IS THIS ROLE RIGHT FOR YOU? We would rather you have a clear picture now than discover it after you join. The role consistently requires the following. If these conditions do not match what you are looking for, this may not be the right fit: Earned scope rather than immediate ownership . Client relationship ownership and independent assessment leadership expand as demonstrated quality and trust are established, not from day one. Working without a defined process . Engagements vary by Solution, client, and Consultant. The role requires building your own structure, workflows, and standards in the absence of fixed procedures. Extensive writing and multiple revision cycles . Writing is an essential function. Deliverables routinely undergo several rounds of substantive feedback and rework before reaching the client. Owning your own project management . The role carries end-to-end accountability for timelines, coordination, and follow-up. Dedicated project management support is not provided. Building internal relationships that influence staffing . Engagement assignments are shaped in part by internal trust and reputation, which the role requires you to actively develop. Capability-based advancement . Progression to Consultant is assessed against a published framework and takes time; it is not tenure-driven or accelerated on request. Limited early opportunity to independently lead assessments . Because our work sits at the C-suite and board level, independent assessment leadership comes later than at firms working deeper in the organization. Influence through partnership rather than sole authority . Decisions are reached collaboratively with Consultants and engagement teams. A distinct business from Executive Search . LAS has different client work, methodologies, and career paths. CRITICAL CAPABILITIES FOR SUCCESS These capabilities form the basis of the LAS Associate Development Framework and of the assessment of performance and promotion readiness. We share them openly so you know what you are signing up for and how you will be evaluated. Project management Manages overall projects and oversees the team's collective efforts to drive the cadence and flow of client outcomes. Owns the project workplan across multiple workstreams; organizes and facilitates team touchpoints and keeps the team accountable Takes ownership of whole projects and serves as a day-to-day point of contact with the client Manages multiple engagements with competing deadlines; sets expectations, clarifies roles, and avoids duplication of effort Anticipates challenges, adjusts priorities, and pushes back internally as appropriate Remains calm under pressure and delivers on commitments, or raises slippage early with a proposed solution Uses technology and AI-enabled tools to improve project efficiency, with appropriate validation Client insights Gathers nuanced insight from sophisticated data collection and delivers it in a way that is relevant for clients and resonates with participants. For any concerns relating to Republic Services’ commitment to equal opportunity employment, you may contact the AWARE Line at 1-866-3-AWARE-4. ABOUT THE COMPANY Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

As our Data Center Manager of Construction (CM MGR), you will be a part of a diverse, upbeat, and creative team tasked with solving fascinating problems constructing Amazon Data Centers. Our data centers are industry-leading examples of energy efficient and cost-effective designs.
You will:
• Own project scope, quality, schedule, and budget for construction of new builds or general capital projects.
• Own construction project management and oversight of construction related activities.
• Work alongside partner teams such as Operations, Networking, Controls, Security, and Commissioning to build Data Centers that directly support our Customers.
• Be a leader in your specific discipline (construction management, building services, architectural, electrical or mechanical engineering).
• Represent Amazon’s owner’s representative on construction sites daily, as, interacting with construction trades.

At Amazon, we are all Owners and leverage unique opportunities presented to us by owning everything from the design review to construction bidding, execution, and final hand-off to our customers. We develop innovative data centers for our Customers.

Key job responsibilities
• Be Amazon’s construction representative on multiple data centers building and capital improvement construction project sites from construction start through hand-off to operations.
• Direct interface with construction general contractors during the construction bidding, award, execution, punch-list, and closeout phases.
• Create construction project Scope of Work (SOW) and Request for Proposals (RFP).
• Conduct negotiations with general contractors and evaluate bids and proposals with detail and accuracy.
• Manage and drive cost, schedule, and quality while managing construction contractors and vendors.
• Perform construction project management activities, including management of documents, submittals, RFIs, change orders, invoices, quality, scope, and schedule.
• Drive construction teams to troubleshoot and perform root-cause failure analysis on equipment failures.
• Support commissioning and integrated system testing and oversight.
• Support operations of installed facilities, including review of procedures, best practices, and maintenance initiatives.
• Support capital request creation.
• Analyze and report construction progress and financials.
• Record and report key construction metrics to team members and management.
• Contribute to construction initiatives aimed at improving construction efficiency and increasing data center resiliency.
• Provide constructability reviews for civil, structural, electrical and mechanical designs for new or optimization of existing data centers.
• Be a leader within the group, and within internal and external data center support teams.

A day in the life
Manage the day to day responsibilities of the CM team, engage with other internal AWS managers and team members. New Carlisle, Indiana will be the permanent reporting location.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. ABOUT THE ROLE

We're seeking a System Software Engineer to join our First-Party Hardware team. In this role, you will design, build, integrate, and validate low-level system software for the manageability and health of OpenAI's first-party AI hardware systems.

You will work across BMC, Linux, firmware interfaces, automation infra, boot and recovery, hardware diagnostics, telemetry, host and platform drivers, network software interfaces, and manufacturing and fleet readiness. A major part of this role is owning the acceptance path for partner-delivered system software: defining requirements, reviewing code and artifacts, reproducing builds, building tests, pushing fixes, and producing the evidence needed for launch decisions.

You will write and review low-level software, debug issues across hardware and software boundaries, build infra and automation to test and manage devices in lab, guide partner deliverables, build validation evidence, and help carry platforms from bring-up through production deployment.

Scopely is looking for a Senior Producer to join the Live Game organisation supporting the MONOPOLY GO! team. This role is remote within the EU and will support our Barcelona and Sevilla hubs.

At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and strive to inspire play every day—through our work alongside talented colleagues and through our connection with millions of players around the world.

MONOPOLY GO! is one of Scopely’s flagship mobile free-to-play franchises and one of the largest games in the mobile industry.

With teams distributed across Barcelona, Sevilla, the United States, and other global locations, this role requires strong production leadership, excellent communication, and exceptional attention to detail.

About the Role

As a Senior Producer within the Live Game organization, you will oversee development across one or more live game workstreams, helping transform product strategy and creative goals into high-quality player experiences.

You will manage development from early planning and team alignment through implementation, integration, QA, release, and live support. This includes coordinating concurrent initiatives, managing complex dependency chains, driving change request flow, and ensuring teams remain focused on delivering meaningful player and business outcomes.

This is a hands-on, in-the-weeds production role requiring both strategic thinking and tactical execution. You will work closely with Product, Design, Engineering, Art, Content, Economy, QA, Localization, Analytics, Live Operations, and Release Management to deliver at the pace and quality expected of a global mobile live-service game.

What You Will Do

• Own the end-to-end production lifecycle for assigned Live Game development workstreams, from discovery and planning through development, release, and post-launch support.
• Manage multiple concurrent initiatives with shared teams, resources, dependencies, and shifting priorities.
• Translate product strategy and roadmap objectives into clear, executable development plans.
• Build and maintain integrated schedules, milestone plans, critical paths, risk registers, and dependency maps.
• Coordinate development across Product, Game Design, Engineering, Art, Content, Economy, QA, Localization, Analytics, Live Operations, and Release Management.
• Establish clear DRIs, requirements, acceptance criteria, decision points, and delivery expectations for major initiatives.
• Manage the complete mobile live-service development lifecycle, including design alignment, implementation, configuration, integration, QA validation, release readiness, live activation, and post-launch follow-up.
• Partner with Live Operations and Release Management to ensure development work is compatible with the LiveOps calendar, release cadence, player priorities, and operational requirements.
• Lead the change request process by assessing the impact of proposed changes on scope, schedule, capacity, quality, risk, and downstream dependencies.
• Drive prioritization and decision-making around change requests, communicate approved changes clearly, and ensure plans and systems remain aligned with the latest direction.
• Proactively identify blockers, bottlenecks, gaps in ownership, and risks to delivery. Resolve issues directly where possible and escalate with clear recommendations when necessary.
• Facilitate milestone reviews, sprint planning, production checkpoints, risk reviews, and cross-functional working sessions.
• Ensure meetings result in clear decisions, owners, deadlines, and follow-through.
• Maintain accurate and current project information across Jira, Airtable, Confluence, and other production systems.
• Communicate project status, risks, dependencies, decisions, and delivery confidence clearly to both senior leadership and development teams across the Barcelona and Sevilla hubs.
• Partner with Live Operations after launch to support issue triage, player-impacting investigations, post-launch actions, and continuous improvement.
• Use player data, team feedback, and operational insights to inform prioritization and improve future development planning.
• Champion improvements to development workflows, production practices, tooling, and cross-functional collaboration across the Live Game organization.

What We’re Looking For

• 5+ years of experience in game production, with significant experience in mobile free-to-play or live-service games.
• Proven experience managing the development and delivery of mobile game features, systems, content, events, or other player-facing experiences.
• Strong understanding of Live Operations, including high-frequency content delivery, live calendars, release cycles, remote configuration, QA validation, launch readiness, and post-launch support.
• Experience managing multiple concurrent development workstreams with complex cross-functional dependencies.
• Strong understanding of roadmap planning, milestone management, critical-path tracking, risk management, change management, and delivery readiness.
• Experience partnering closely with Engineering and technical teams, with an understanding of client/server dependencies, configuration, integration, and mobile release considerations.
• Demonstrated ability to manage dependency escalation, negotiate tradeoffs, and create accountability across teams.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to bring clarity to complex or ambiguous situations.
• Exceptional attention to detail and a strong sense of ownership for the quality and accuracy of production information.
• Proficiency with tools such as Jira, Airtable, Confluence, Google Workspace, or similar project-management systems.
• Ability to operate at both strategic and tactical levels, from shaping a development roadmap to following individual deliverables through completion.
• A player-focused mindset and passion for building engaging, polished, and continuously evolving mobile game experiences.

The Ideal Candidate

• Is highly organized, structured, dependable, and comfortable operating in a high-volume Live Operations environment.
• Understands the realities of mobile free-to-play development, including rapid iteration, global releases, frequent content updates, live player impact, and operational precision.
• Drives outcomes beyond task tracking and status reporting.
• Anticipates problems before they become delivery issues.
• Communicates directly, diplomatically, and consistently across global teams and time zones.
• Creates accountability without unnecessary process or bureaucracy.
• Is comfortable challenging unclear plans, identifying gaps, and driving decisions.
• Can manage competing priorities while maintaining focus on the critical path.
• Brings sound judgment, energy, and a collaborative mindset to a fast-paced, globally distributed development organization.
• Cares deeply about both the quality of the player experience and the operational excellence required to deliver it.

About Scopely

Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.

Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.

Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.
